prerequisites: Mechanical and structural characterization of materials

learning_outcomes.text: The student will acquire an in-depth knowledge of the principles and evolution of additive technologies, understanding the AM process chain and the main physical mechanisms of the different processes (material extrusion, powder bed fusion, binder jetting, etc.). The concepts of Design for Additive Manufacturing (DFAM) and the paradigms of shape, hierarchical, functional and material complexity, as well as the fundamentals of advanced prototyping and digital manufacturing, will also be introduced.
Identify and select the most suitable additive process according to the material, geometry and application of the component.
Design and optimize a component according to the rules of Design for Additive Manufacturing, using CAD/CAE tools and topological optimization and generative design software.
Develop and validate an experimental or simulative design on a component produced using additive manufacturing, evaluating the mechanical, thermal or functional performance of the component.

The student will develop the ability to critically evaluate the technological and design solutions related to additive manufacturing, analyzing the advantages and limitations compared to traditional subtractive processes. They will be able to consider the aspects of sustainability, efficiency, cost and innovation in their design and process choices.

The student will be able to communicate clearly and professionally, using the technical language of additive technologies, both in written form (technical reports, projects) and oral (presentation and discussion of papers). He will also be able to interact effectively with designers, technologists and researchers in the industrial and academic context.

The course will provide the methodological bases to autonomously deepen the issues related to additive manufacturing, generative design and the digitization of production processes, favoring the ability to update with respect to technological evolutions and industrial trends of Industry 4.0

syllabus_topics: DEFINITION, HISTORY, AND PRINCIPLES OF ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING
PRINCIPLES OF LAYER-BY-LAYER MACHINING. ADVANTAGES AND LIMITATIONS OF ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING. GENERALIZED AM PROCESS CHAIN.
INDUSTRIAL MATERIALS AND APPLICATIONS: RAPID PROTOTYPING, RAPID PRINTING, DIRECT DIGITAL PRODUCTION.
OVERVIEW OF THE TRANSITIONS BETWEEN GREEN AND DIGITAL AND THE ROLE OF AM
CASE STUDIES SHOWING THE IMPACT OF AM IN DIFFERENT INDUSTRIES.
OVERVIEW OF AM PROCESSES ON POLYMERS (E.G., STEREOLITHOGRAPHY, FUSED FILAMENT FABRICATION, TANK PHOTOPOLYMERIZATION, POLYJET PROCESSES, MATERIAL JETTING, BINDER JETTING).
ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING MATERIALS: LIQUID-BASED MATERIALS, POWDER-BASED MATERIALS, SOLID-BASED MATERIALS, METAL POWDER CHARACTERISTICS, PROPERTIES, AND APPLICATIONS.
PROCESS PARAMETERS, PROCESS DESIGN, CONTROL AND OPTIMIZATION.
AM-SPECIFIC DESIGN GUIDELINES AND CHALLENGES FOR POLYMERS, ENGINEERING PLASTICS, AND COMPOSITES.
ENERGY SOURCES: LASER BEAM AND ELECTRON BEAM TECHNOLOGY, ELECTRIC ARC AND PLASMA TECHNOLOGIES.

ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING PROCESSES OF METALS (E.G., POWDER BED FUSION, DIRECTED ENERGY DEPOSITION, WIRE ARC ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING, SELECTIVE LASER MELTING, SELECTIVE LASER SINTERING, ELECTRON BEAM MELTING, BINDER JETTING, THICK FILM DEPOSITION)
SELECTION, PROPERTIES AND APPLICATIONS OF THE METAL MATERIAL.
PROCESS PARAMETERS, PROCESS DESIGN, PROCESS CONTROL AND OPTIMIZATION.
DESIGN PRINCIPLES AND CONSTRAINTS IN THE USE OF METAL-BASED AM.
AM PRODUCT VERIFICATION.
DIMENSIONAL AND GEOMETRIC METROLOGY FOR AM
VOLUME-BASED MEASUREMENT SYSTEMS: 3D X-RAY COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY.
IN-SITU AND IN-LINE QUALITY MONITORING: SOLUTIONS AND PERSPECTIVES.
HEAT TREATMENTS AND FINISHES
THERMO-MECHANICAL PERFORMANCE OF COMPONENTS MADE USING ADDITIVE TECHNIQUES.
USING COMMERCIAL CAD/CAM SOFTWARE (FUSION 360)
3D PRINTING: CAD MODEL, CONSTRUCTION OF STL FILES AND OBJECTS
PRACTICAL ACTIVITIES IN THE LABORATORY
teaching_methods: Development of individual or group projects

assessment_methods.method: Oral test on topics covered in lessons
Discussion and evaluation of the technical report

assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by the sum of the oral exam grade, up to a maximum of 40%, and the technical report grade, up to a maximum of 60% of the overall grade. If a student achieves the maximum grade (30 out of 30), honors may be awarded at the discretion of the teacher to students demonstrating autonomous processing skills and logical connection between course topics.
